actions.solution: In src/data/comparisons.ts entry simple-ira-vs-401k: (1) add a comparison-table row 'Early withdrawal tax before 59 1/2' (SIMPLE IRA: 10%, 25% in the first 2 years of participation; 401(k): 10%, plus an exception for leaving the sponsoring employer in or after the year you turn 55); (2) insert section 2 'Withdrawal and Rollover Rules: SIMPLE IRA vs 401(k)' (25% window, SIMPLE-to-SIMPLE-only rollover in the window, Roth rollover after 2 years is taxable, age-55 exception limited to the sponsoring employer and not for IRAs, usual exceptions, neither plan suits money needed before 59 1/2, employees usually cannot pick the plan; IRS-attributed; link /compare/traditional-ira-vs-simple-ira/); (3) insert section 3 'Who Can Sponsor and Who Must Be Included' from the IRS SIMPLE FAQ (100-employee limit, $5,000 pay tests, no opt out of participation, one-plan rule) to reach the 1,500-word comparison floor with sourced substance, no padding; (4) add two FAQs (early-withdrawal difference; who is eligible); (5) correct EVERY location that calls the match mandatory/unskippable: intro 'capped near 3% of pay'; table cell 'Employer contribution'; verdict 'mandatory 3% match every year'; heading and paragraphs 1 and 2 of 'The employer cost you can't skip' ('no year where you can choose to skip it', 'a mandatory 3% obligation in a slow year'); FAQ 'Does a SIMPLE IRA require an employer match?' ('mandatory every year'). Keep: employer must still contribute a match (normally up to 3%) or 2% nonelective; match may drop to no lower than 1% in up to 2 of 5 years with notice. actions.answer: The page's table and intro already list seven differences; the missing ones are that a SIMPLE IRA charges 25% instead of 10% on money taken out in its first 2 years and allows only SIMPLE-to-SIMPLE rollovers then, while a 401(k) has the 10% rule plus an age-55 separation exception, and that the SIMPLE match can drop to 1% in up to 2 of 5 years (list).
